atomic_facts.fact: Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to violating the Bank Secrecy Act.
The charge to which Zhao pleaded guilty is a money laundering charge (failure to maintain an adequate anti-money-laundering program).
Changpeng Zhao was sentenced to four months in prison.
Zhao's prison sentence was not approximately four years.
The length of Changpeng Zhao's prison sentence was four months.
Changpeng Zhao was released from custody on Friday, September 27, 2024 (two days ahead of his scheduled Sunday, Sep. 29 release date).
Changpeng Zhao received a presidential pardon from Donald Trump.
The pardon was granted in October 2025.
Nearly 1,700 British investors filed a £150 million UK High Court claim against Binance and Changpeng Zhao.
The claim concerns allegedly unauthorized leveraged crypto derivatives sold in breach of UK financial law.
The claim remained ongoing as of around July 2026 (Reuters reported on 2026-06-30 that the investors 'are suing' Binance and Zhao).
The pardon did not extinguish civil liability, since the High Court claim against Zhao personally was filed/active after his October 2025 pardon.
